appraisal_events.evidence: disant d'ailleurs en riant à propos de son frère : « Il est dans les tranchées, ils sont à trente mètres des Boches ! » jusqu'à ce qu'ayant appris qu'il l'était lui-même on l'eût mis dans un camp de concentration.
appraisal_events.explanation: The director's boastful, xenophobic patriotism about his brother is comically undercut when the brother turns out to be German himself and is interned, exposing the director's hypocrisy and misjudgment.

appraisal_events.evidence: Le pauvre Vaugoubert... a été sept fois blessé avant d'être tué... C'était un être charmant. ... ont empêché les Allemands de passer.
appraisal_events.explanation: In his letter, which the narrator frames as wholly sympathetic, Saint-Loup elevates Vaugoubert as a modest, charming hero whose repeated wounds and death helped hold the line against the Germans.

appraisal_events.evidence: Saint-Loup, lui, beaucoup plus intelligent et artiste, restait intelligent et artiste... / la lettre... était... entièrement sympathique.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly praises Saint-Loup's genuine artistic sensibility and liberal culture, contrasting him favorably with mediocre wartime versifiers, and calls his letter wholly sympathetic.

status_effects.explanation: His patriotic boasting is comically deflated by the revelation that his own brother was German and interned.
He is elevated as a charming, repeatedly wounded hero whose death is framed as meaningful sacrifice.
The narrator's direct praise of his intelligence, artistic taste, and sympathetic letter locally elevates him.

ambiguities: The 'Vaugoubert' praised in Saint-Loup's letter is explicitly 'le fils de l'ambassadeur' (the ambassador's son), not M. de Vaugoubert himself; the candidate/alias entry may conflate father and son, and the grieving father is referenced only as 'le pauvre père' without being separately named or scored.

The narrator raises two possible readings of Gilberte's admiring account of the German officers' good manners (contagion of the Guermantes' Bavarian aristocratic ties, versus an antisemitic 'internationalisme juif' explanation), explicitly deferring judgment ('ce qui n'aurait probablement pas été juste, comme on verra'). This discredit/prestige-association question is left locally unresolved and was not scored, to avoid overreading a self-flagged, unstable ambiguity.
